question: On newest-four growth, which never ends, does the not-all-equal law cut, count or fold the line: how does the least bond containing two distinctions behave as their distance along the line grows, at closing probabilities 0 to 0.9?

definitions.bases: fates.proc_band(w = 4) at q in {0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9}, ten bases each, grown to 800 distinctions; seeds sha256 C:q:base:grow.
definitions.pairs: eight nested sequences per base: i uniform in [40, 200]; j = i + g + r, g in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512}, r uniform in {0..3}; seeds sha256 C:q:base:pairs.
definitions.least bond: bonddp.least_bond, exact, members within [i - 8, j + 8], no size cap, blow-up past 20,000 states; undefined = no bond with members in that window.
definitions.open windows: positions m in [i + 3, j] whose distinctions m - 3 .. m do not carry all four knots.
definitions.rechecks: up to five undefined pairs at g >= 64 and four defined pairs per base with margin 32; bonds of at most ten members verified by SAT.

public_inputs.code: census.py (sha256 54d62f8be665ae8b560c082b34938a99185bb8edfdf3a11509013dcd679ed9ba) and bonddp.py (sha256 8bc70ca09b96ed24689a828297671302dc3f8895617d764b1ea3823aea7eb608) beside this file; fates.py of RANDOM-FATES-20261112-001A-E001 (sha256 72d3571ed66dddaa6c517b3ce29ce14ae72c008c025669e2ef071b77b73eba35); pysat; 6 workers.
public_inputs.run: census.py from the repository root, then census.py --summary; output artifacts/RANDOM-FATES-20261112-001C/RANDOM-FATES-20261112-001C-E001_newest_four_count/.

forbidden_inputs: Changing bases, pairs, margins, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: Per (q, g): share of pairs with a bond, base medians of L, steps apart, open windows.
cheapest_meaningful_control: The complete pattern (L = 2 at g = 0 mod 4, else 3), the chain {2k, 2k+1, 2k+2} (L = steps + 2), the programme against brute force on 300 small patterns, SAT verification of small bonds.

predictions.Q1: median over bases of g_half (least g with fewer than half of eight pairs defined) strictly rising over q = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and at most 128 at q = 0.1.
predictions.Q2: q = 0.5: among bases with at least six of eight defined at g = 32, 64, 128, the ratio (L128 - L64)/(L64 - L32) of base medians in [1.5, 2.7] in at least 7 bases.
predictions.Q3: g = 64: median of base medians of L strictly falling over q = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 (bases with at least four of eight defined).
predictions.Q4a: q = 0.7 and 0.9, g = 256, defined pairs (at least 20): Spearman correlation of L with open windows above 0.5.
predictions.Q4b: q = 0.9: base median L at g = 512 at least 3 above that at g = 128 in at least 8 of 10 bases.

decision_rules.Q1 holds: rare closings cut the line into pieces that lengthen with q
decision_rules.Q2 and Q3 hold: the law counts linearly in a unit that shrinks with closings
decision_rules.Q4b fails: near the complete pattern the line folds
decision_rules.a control fails: a bug; the run is not interpreted until fixed

stop_rule: One run and its summary; one referee pass; report.
runtime: About ten minutes on 6 workers; systemd-run --user -p MemoryMax=16G -p MemorySwapMax=0.
